Rachel Brooks is a Los Angeles-based multidisciplinary artist whose work explores the narratives of the human figure through watercolor and charcoal — bodies rendered as feeling rather than form, dissolving between abstraction and presence.

These three works are archival prints from her Stearns series — a collection of small works in watercolor and ink described by the artist as highly experimental studio practice works that inspire and inform her larger series. The figures move between representation and abstraction, faces and bodies emerging and dissolving in washes of color.

From a personal collection. The artist has been a close friend since our University of Michigan days.
